transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-25
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood CSM), Marta Reyes (Pinnacle Head of ML), Devon Carter (Pinnacle Cloud Architect), Liam O'Neill (Pinnacle Procurement), Sana Patel (Pinnacle Security)

Summary:
Quick renewal check-in focused on capacity upgrades and expansion to APAC regions; discussion on contract extension length and pricing tiers for dedicated pools; security and compliance follow-ups (SOC2, KMS, VPC). Agreed next steps: pricing + contract draft, benchmark run, security deep-dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for making time, uh this is Alex from Redwood, i'll kick off real quick, are we good to record?
[00:18] Marta: yes go ahead, thanks Alex, hey everyone.
[00:22] Priya: morning all, Priya here - i'll cover the capacity and perf pieces.
[00:28] Devon: hi, Devon. Quick note we have to keep this under 45, liam's got another.
[00:34] Alex: perfect, quick agenda — renewal timeline, capacity needs (dedicated), regions (APAC add), security asks, pricing / contract extension.
[00:43] Liam: sounds good. procurement wants a 12- or 24-month option to lock pricing.
[00:49] Marta: we also want to increase reserved capacity during weekday peak windows for inference pipelines, mostly autocomplete and scoring. current spikes are killing our p95.
[01:05] Priya: got it, do you have numbers for the p95 tail? like tokens/sec or req/sec during peaks?
[01:12] Marta: roughly 1.2k reqs/minute at peak for the scoring pipeline, avg sequence ~120 tokens. latency SLO target p95 < 250ms.
[01:23] Priya: okay that helps. So two levers: increase Dedicated GPU pool and apply smarter batching + prefix caching. We saw a 30-40% cost drop on similar footprints with caching enabled.
[01:38] Devon: are there any tradeoffs with latency when enabling more aggressive batching? we can't exceed 250ms p95.
[01:45] Priya: good question. Our continuous batching is workload-aware; for strict p95 we can set a max batch latency of like 30ms so you get batching benefits on the tail but we keep the SLO. For very bursty spikes, we provision burst capacity too.
[02:02] Marta: and the burst is billed differently, right? how do we model that into committed capacity?
[02:09] Alex: yes, burst is metered; our proposal will show committed baseline + burst discounts. procurement liam?
[02:16] Liam: we prefer predictable monthly commit with a small burst buffer. 10-15% burst looks reasonable.
[02:22] Alex: noted. we'll model 12 vs 24 month pricing with two commit tiers and a 10% burst buffer example.
[02:30] Sana: quick security question — KMS integration and key ownership. we need to ensure customer-controlled keys for model payloads and logs.
[02:39] Alex: absolutely, we support customer-managed keys via KMS and HSM integrations. logs can be redacted and encrypted at rest. we'll share the KMS integration doc.
[02:48] Sana: do you have any gotchas with private deployments vs hosted for data residency? we may prefer Private in APAC if latency/regulatory.
[02:58] Priya: Private gives you full VPC and residency control; however, deployment lead time is longer. For faster time-to-value in APAC, we can spin up dedicated hosted capacity in region with SOC2 controls, but for regulated data Private is recommended.
[03:13] Devon: timeline — how long to add a new region with Dedicated? like APAC region - singapore?
[03:19] Priya: Typically 4-6 weeks if it's a hosted dedicated pool in a new region, faster if we already have capacity there. Private deployment to a customer VPC is 8-12 weeks depending on procurement and network setup.
[03:33] Marta: we want both options: start with hosted dedicated in SG for Q2, roadmap to Private later this year if compliance requires.
[03:40] Alex: that fits the playbook. we'll include migration path and estimated timelines in the quote.
[03:45] Liam: on contract extension length, we like the 24 month for price certainty but need exit clauses if usage is < 60% of commit.
[03:54] Alex: we can include flex clauses: true-up and a partial refund or credit if usage deviates significantly. we'll propose an SLA and a usage threshold clause.
[04:03] Priya: quick perf note — we recommend quantization profile X for your model family to save ~20% GPU memory, which helps with denser packing. will that affect quality?
[04:12] Marta: we can tolerate very small quality delta, but not more than 2% on our evaluation metric.
[04:18] Priya: we'll run a regression eval during the benchmark run to show any delta.
[04:24] Devon: networking — we need a Network Flow diagram for Private. i'll share our VPC peering requirements.
[04:30] Alex: add that to action items.
[04:33] [05:00] Jordan: hey team, small thing on billing — can we get monthly usage breakdown by model, route and token type? helps us show finance.
[05:08] Alex: yep that's in Console; we can also send a sample billing export and a per-token cost table.
[05:15] Marta: on competitors, we did a POC with MegaCloud AI last quarter; Megacloud had better latency raw but cost was 40% higher. Redwood was easiest to integrate.
[05:30] Priya: good to know. i'll note relevant perf tradeoffs in the proposal.
[05:36] Sana: security again — we need SOC2 + ISO baseline and pen-test reports, plus SSO via SAML and RBAC.
[05:46] Alex: we have SOC2 and ISO documentation; pen test summaries we can share; SSO SAML and RBAC are supported now. we'll send security artifacts and schedule a technical deep-dive with your Security team.
[05:57] Sana: can we also have audit logs exported to our SIEM?
[06:03] Priya: audit logs available via our logging endpoints and can forward to your SIEM or S3 bucket.
[06:10] Devon: about data retention — we require logs to be retained for 12 months and some payload retention rules. is that doable?
[06:17] Alex: yes retention policies configurable per account; we'll include that in the security doc.
[06:22] [08:00] Marta: ok turning to benchmarks, when can we run an end-to-end test using our payloads?
[08:08] Priya: we can schedule bench run early next week; we'll need a sample dataset, traffic shape, and auth token to hit the test harness.
[08:16] Marta: i'll share sample traces and the test corpus today.
[08:20] Priya: great, we'll provision a staging dedicated pool that mirrors the proposed sizing and run p95/p99 tests and regression eval.
[08:29] Devon: one more on regions — which APAC POPs do you have? Singapore, tokyo?
[08:35] Alex: we have SG, tokyo, sydney in our hosted catalog; Singapore is best for low-latency SEA traffic. For Private we can deploy to your on-prem cluster or cloud region in ap-southeast-1 if you prefer.
[08:47] Liam: procurement wants pricing for SG hosted vs Private in ap-southeast-1.
[08:52] Alex: we'll include both line items and migration assumptions.
[08:56] [10:00] Marta: curious about rollback and canary for model upgrades — if we pin versions, how do you handle rollouts across regions?
[10:08] Priya: we have rollout policies: canary traffic, A/B, auto-fallback to earlier model variants if latency spikes or error rates increase. cross-region rollouts are supported and you can pin per-region.
[10:21] Marta: good — we need that for regulated models.
[10:24] Alex: Priya will include the rollout policy notes in the technical appendix.
[10:28] [12:00] Sana: about encryption in transit — do you support mTLS between customer VPC and Redwood private endpoints?
[12:06] Priya: yes, mTLS for Private + TLS for hosted endpoints, and we can enable client certs for stricter environments.
[12:14] Sana: ok thanks.
[12:18] Devon: any known limits for KV cache size on Dedicated pools? our scoring uses long-context caching.
[12:26] Priya: KV cache is configurable; with quantization and recommended kernels we support large KV caches. we'll capture recommended instance types in the bench plan.
[12:36] [15:00] Liam: tldr on pricing — can you present a 12-month and 24-month committed option with tiered discounts and a 10% burst example?
[15:10] Alex: yes — 12-month with x% discount, 24-month with y% savings and an exit clause; will model usage thresholds.
[15:18] Liam: great. also include enterprise support SLA and response times.
[15:23] Alex: yes, enterprise support is add-on; we'll show both standard and premium SLA.
[15:29] [18:00] Jordan: quick CSM note — we'll schedule quarterly QBRs post-renewal, and Jordan will be the point contact for onboarding.
[18:08] Jordan: hi all, happy to run the onboarding plan.
[18:12] Marta: thanks.
[18:15] [20:00] Priya: ok wrapping up, action items and timeline — Alex will send pricing/contract draft, Priya will run bench, security will get SOC2/KMS deep-dive with Sana.
[20:26] Marta: timeline wise we want commitment by end of month to hit Q2 capacity needs.
[20:32] Alex: understoood, we'll aim to get draft by 3/28.
[20:36] Devon: and we'll provide region/legal requirements by 3/27.
[20:42] Alex: perfect. any final questions?
[20:45] Marta: none from me. thanks everyone.
[20:48] Liam: none.
[20:50] Sana: thanks.
[20:52] Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and docs.
[21:00] End of meeting.
